newsitem.title: USA: Disagreements reported to endanger Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: Disagreements reported to endanger Mideast summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived at the White House on Wednesday for more talks with President Bill Clinton and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu amid reports the Middle East summit had reached stalemate.

Palestinian sources in Jerusalem said Palestinian negotiators had rejected a series of Israeli demands, and CNN quoted top Arafat adviser Nabil Shaath as saying: "It's finished. We didn't agree on one thing. All of the problems still remain."

U.S. officials, speaking after a morning of talks at the State Department among Secretary of State Warren Christopher and top aides to Arafat and Netanyahu, were less pessimistic, noting the talks were still going on.
"We're in the midst of a negotiation here. People will say things to the press" to try to advance their own cause, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

He said: "There are still problems and issues that divide them. We're offering ideas," but he added that the tone of the talks on Wednesday, which followed a marathon sesion between Arafat and Netanyahu at the White House on Tuesday, was "quite constructive".

One well-informed Palestine Liberation Organisation official told Reuters in Jerusalem: "There is a crisis in Washington because of Israeli demands that have been rejected by the Palestinians. Netanyahu asked for a meeting with Arafat. Arafat has rejected. The Americans are intervening and mediating to contain the crisis."
